measures.what_it_does: Lifts Timberland Regional Library's regular property tax levy from about $0.22 to $0.35 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 and 2028; the 2028 amount becomes the base for later limits. TRL says it would keep hours, staff and collections after a $3.8 million shortfall and 2026 layoffs. Voters in all five TRL counties decide it; all of Pacific County is in the district.
measures.cost_line: From $0.228924 to $0.35 per $1,000 of assessed value. TRL estimates $31 a year on the $239,100 median Pacific County home; the explanatory statement gives about $40 a year on a $334,000 home.
measures.pro_summary: Supporters say the levy has not risen in 25 years and the increase is 'a long overdue cost-of-living raise' that would restore hours and staffing.
measures.con_summary: Opponents say households already face rising levies and the library should cut costs, seek grants and manage existing money better first; 'Voting No is not a vote against libraries or literacy.'

taxes.basis: A yes vote is a levy lid lift, named in the taxes pole_b, raising TRL's regular rate by more than half, from $0.228924 to $0.35 per $1,000.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7284 (S1); TRL levy page (S2); Chinook Observer/Thurston Chronicle coverage of the trustees' decision (S3); PDC committee query (S4).

measures.what_it_does: Renews the North Pacific County EMS District's one-year excess levy for 2027 to subsidize ambulance and emergency medical service in the Naselle, Nemah, Bay Center, South Bend, Raymond and Willapa Valley areas. The district covers Pacific County outside the Ocean Beach, Ocosta and North River school districts. Needs 60% approval.
measures.cost_line: $0.40 per $1,000 of assessed value, no more than $800,000, collected in 2027 only (about $96 on a $240,000 property).
measures.pro_summary: The district says the levy replaces the expiring 2026 levy and keeps current ambulance service levels through 2027; voters renewed it with 73.6% in 2025.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote approves an excess property tax levy, but it renews an expiring one-year levy that voters have approved annually, so +1.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7388 (S1); SOS results for the 2025, 2024 and 2020 renewals (S2-S4); PDC committee query (S5).

measures.what_it_does: Raises Fire District 3's regular property tax levy to up to $0.61 per $1,000 for 2027 collection; that levy becomes the base for later limits. The district serves Menlo, Lebam, Frances, Baleville, Elk Horn Flats, Old Willapa and East Raymond and says revenue growth of about 1.76% a year has fallen behind costs.
measures.cost_line: Up to $0.61 per $1,000 of assessed value in 2027, a $0.20 increase per the district (about $48 more a year on a $240,000 property).
measures.pro_summary: The district's board says the increase keeps its current fire protection service levels for the near future.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote is a levy lid lift (taxes pole_b) raising the district's rate by about half, to $0.61 per $1,000.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7389 (S1); SOS 2025 results (S2); PDC committee query (S3). No local news coverage found.

measures.what_it_does: Restores Fire District 6's regular property tax levy to $0.50 per $1,000 for 2027 collection and lets levy revenue grow up to 6% a year (capped at $1.50 per $1,000) for the next five years; the 2031 levy becomes the base for later limits. The district, around Bay Center, says the levy is its main funding source.
measures.cost_line: $0.50 per $1,000 of assessed value in 2027, then up to 6% more levy revenue a year through 2032 collection (about $120 a year on a $240,000 property at $0.50).
measures.pro_summary: The district says approval would let it 'significantly improve and expand' fire and emergency services.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote is a levy lid lift (taxes pole_b) that restores the rate to $0.50 and allows up to 6% yearly growth for five years instead of 1%.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA guide record 7391 (S1); SOS 2025 results (S2); PDC committee query (S3). No local news coverage found.
